answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is locked until it completes a randomly assigned task, with tasks drawn from a public beacon and verified by peers whose own stakes are slashed for approving fabricated work. An attacker can still create many keys, but must tie up real capital for each one and risks losing it when the identities echo one another or fail independent checks; an ivory token or copied profile alone buys no influence.
